analogs.covers: Social life: lifelong pairs, peaceful flocks on the water, pairs that split off to nest, fierce parents
Body: a humped, gangly giant that wades and dives for water plants and strikes with its forelimbs

headline: A lifelong swan pair in a moose's body: a gentle lake giant and fierce parent that splashes predators away.

setting.label: Lakes, rivers and coasts
setting.note: Sedentary semi-aquatic. Spends its life near water with other pairs: swimming and diving for food, foraging shores for fruit and shellfish, chewing lakeweed, and retreating into the water when harassed.

playsLike: You are an Apex semi-aquatic herbivore (5,500 combat weight) that pairs for life. Unpaired adults gather in big peaceful 'gatherings' of spinster and bachelor flocks, and pairs split off to nest, with both parents defending the young. You chase off Large-or-smaller carnivores, but flee Spinosaurus and avoid Apex carnivores. Near water you rear up and slam the surface to soak and spook land predators.

why.text: Lifelong pairbonds sealed by a gifted rock the pair bury together. Mute swans famously pair for life (official inspiration: swans).
Unlimited peaceful 'gatherings' with a spinster flock and bachelor flocks, while pairs split off to nest. Non-breeding swans flock the same way.
Both parents defend offspring together, and it may chase away Large-tier carnivores. Swans are notorious nest defenders.
Swims and dives for food and chews lakeweed all day. Moose wade and dive for aquatic plants.
A humped back, long snout and massive clawed forelimbs slammed down in defence, like a moose striking with its front hooves.

notLike: Moose are solitary; Deinocheirus is highly social.
Swans chase off intruders; Deinocheirus calmly retreats into the water from other herbivores.
twist: The hippo (official inspiration) supplies the idea of a bulky animal that uses water as its refuge, but Deinocheirus has a far calmer temper.
